p0_closure.mechanism: While a valid final issue to the same row is recoverably stalled by psum_write_ready=0, the wrapper fail-closes prefetch_valid and prefetch_ready. On release, the unchanged sealed r1 core performs the existing exact same-cycle RAW forward.

p1_findings.finding: The wrapper adds a combinational path from prefetch_valid, issue_valid/last, row IDs and psum_write_ready to prefetch_ready. Static dependency review and a 32-row Boolean concurrency table found no internal ready feedback loop, but the source must obey the standard rule that valid/payload do not depend combinationally on ready.
p1_findings.required_action: Run the r2 top under the exact same 3.000 ns pre-macro DC constraints and compare timing/area against the sealed r1 top. A timing failure or materially worse critical path forbids performance admission. Full-controller integration must check that no external valid-ready loop is formed.

p1_findings.finding: The r2 producer run is intentionally targeted. It has nonzero stalled-hazard, release-forward, output-stall and back-to-back covers, but macro-read, read-response, dual-enqueue, queue-full, full-consume and overflow covers are zero. Those paths remain validated in the sealed unchanged r1 core, not dynamically re-executed through the wrapper.
p1_findings.required_action: Before Formality/full-controller admission, either rerun the full r1 concurrency suite through the r2 wrapper or prove transparency whenever stalled_raw_hazard_w=0. This does not block a cost-only same-constraint DC compare.

p1_findings.finding: The guard keys on !psum_write_ready. Other final non-ready causes remain governed by the sealed core's terminal ID/overflow fault contract; the wrapper must not be described as a general pending-write coherence mechanism.
p1_findings.required_action: Keep the claim limited to the reproduced psum-backpressure P0 and retain the existing fail-stop assertions for illegal metadata/overflow cases.
